blocks.text: Exact Data Matching (EDM) is an advanced data loss prevention (DLP) technique that finds specific data values that are important to the organization and need to be protected rather than finding general data patterns or formats only. For example, an organization can detect the exact match of a customer's credit card number, rather than detecting only the pattern, to enhance detection accuracy and reduce false positives.

Using Exact Data Match (EDM) index templates allows the Zscaler service to identify a record from a structured data source that matches predefined criteria. In either case, identifying and correlating multiple tokens that contribute to a particular record, to identify ownership of that data, is crucial. To learn more, see Understanding Exact Data Match Index Templates and About Exact Data Match.
The following is the EDM workflow:

blocks.item: Use the Index Tool and Configure EDM:

Create EDM entries using the Index Tool. Follow the same process as inline web DLP, as the rule evaluation for endpoint EDM occurs in the cloud. Define a dictionary with the EDM type, add it to a DLP engine, and select it within your Endpoint DLP rules. To learn more, see Creating an Exact Data Match Template.
Configure EDM on the Endpoint Data Scan page:

Authorize Users to Run the Optimizer Tool: Go to Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information > Exact Data Match (EDM) > Settings and assign user permissions to run the EDM Optimizer. To learn more, see About Endpoint Data Scan Sensitive Information: Exact Data Match.

Enable EDM Settings: On the Endpoint Settings page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Configuration > Endpoint Settings), enable Continuous Classification and EDM settings, then activate the policy. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint Settings.
Create the Prefilter Criteria on the Endpoint Using the EDM Optimizer:
Launch EDM Optimizer: On an endpoint used by an authorized user, right-click the CSV file used for indexing and select Zscaler> EDM Optimizer.
See image.
You must use the exact same CSV file that was uploaded to the Index Tool.

Select Columns and Define Column Types: Select at least three columns to serve as the prefiltering criteria. Designate each column as either a Dictionary (for named entities) or a Regular Expression (for pattern-based data like IDs). Using Regular Expressions improves performance when data, such as a Customer ID, follows a predictable pattern.
Validate and Create EDM: Click Create Exact Data Matching. The tool validates that the selected column types match at least 90% of the CSV data to ensure accuracy.
See image.

If the match rate is below 90%, then you must fine-tune the regular expression, switch to a dictionary type, or select different columns. The tool generates the local prefiltering criteria file after validation.
Activation and Distribution:
Activate the Prefilter File: After the EDM file is created via the optimizer, the admin must activate the newly created EDM.
See image.
Distribute to Endpoints: After the EDM is activated, the EDM prefilter criteria are automatically pushed to all managed endpoints.
Inspection and Enforcement:
Continuous Classification: As part of the continuous classification scan, Endpoint DLP evaluates the prefilter criteria. If a file matches these criteria, then it is flagged as an EDM candidate.
Cloud Inspection: Flagged candidate files are sent to the cloud for full EDM inspection. After the cloud confirms a match, the classification result is stored locally on the endpoint.

Policy Enforcement: The endpoint uses the stored classification to enforce DLP policies across supported channels (i.e., removable storage, network shares, personal cloud storage, application file access and printing). Enforcement works even when the device is offline.
EDM is not supported for Clipboard.
Printing is only supported on Windows when using Microsoft Office or Adobe Reader.
